title: Uniswap v4 instances add a fourth control category: where on the price curve liquidity may be placed
content:
The Uniswap v4 instances restate the `Rate Limits` header again, now listing five parameter families: "The current `maxAmount`, `slope`, slippage, **ticks, and fee** for this conduit's inflow/outflow/swap" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.11.1.2.4, repeated at .11.2.2.4, .11.3.2.4, .11.4.2.4). Each instance then carries a `Tick Range and Width` document — for PYUSD/USDS: "Min lower tick limit: 276,314 (-0.1%), Max upper tick limit: 276,334 (+0.1%), Max tick width: 10 ticks" (.11.1.2.4.5) — and a `Swap Fee` of 0.0005% (.11.1.2.4.6).

Concentrated liquidity makes position geometry a first-class risk decision. An LP position in v4 exists only across a chosen tick interval; outside it the position converts entirely into one of the two assets and stops earning. Choosing the interval is therefore choosing both the yield and the failure mode, and it cannot be expressed as an amount.

The control set has now grown across four venue types in a clear progression: lending needed quantity only; AMM swapping added price tolerance; concentrated-liquidity AMMs add position range and fee tier. Each new instrument type has required the Instance Configuration Document to learn a new vocabulary rather than reuse the existing one.

The governance significance is that the tick bounds are stated as *limits* — 'min lower', 'max upper', 'max width' — not as the current position. Governance authorises a region within which the operator may place and adjust liquidity, the same delegation-within-a-band pattern used for the savings yield ceiling, applied here to where capital may sit on a price curve.
description: Beyond quantity and slippage, each v4 pool specifies Tick Range and Width plus a Swap Fee — concentrated liquidity forces governance to authorize position geometry, not just size.
